_hinweis: Vocabulary step on /teachers/lesson and /lesson: for each A1 word field in kursinhalte.json (bloecke[].wortschatz, keys must match exactly) a task for the learners and its words. A word that is a lemma of the A1 list (src/content/lexicon/a1.json) gets its article (un / une for nouns that elide), plural and example sentence from there; a noun the list does not have may be written with its article ("la carte Vitale"); phrases without an entry (Bonjour !, letters) are shown as written here. Word fields without an entry only show the general task. French text carries a no-break space before ? ! : (written \u00a0).

frCA.note: Québec: courriel for e-mail, cellulaire for portable, char for voiture, déjeuner / dîner / souper for breakfast / lunch / dinner, fin de semaine for week-end.

Greetings: bonjour, bonsoir, salut.aufgabe: Walk around the room. Say hello to three people, ask how they are and say goodbye: once with tu, once with vous. In France you say bonjour first, even in a shop or a lift.

Countries and nationalities.aufgabe: Ask your partner: « Tu viens d'où ? » – « Je viens du Maroc / de Syrie / d'Ukraine. » Show the country on a map or on your phone.

Languages.aufgabe: Ask each other: « Tu parles quelles langues ? » Everyone says two languages. Write all the languages of the class on the board. Languages are masculine and have no capital letter: le français, l'arabe.

The alphabet and spelling.aufgabe: Spell your first name and your surname. Your partner writes them down and reads them back. Say the accents too: e accent aigu, c cédille.
woerter: Vous pouvez épeler, s'il vous plaît ?

Numbers.aufgabe: Count round the class to 20, then in tens to 100: soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix. In pairs, dictate three phone numbers to each other. In France people read them in pairs: 06 12 34 56 78 = zéro six, douze, trente-quatre, cinquante-six, soixante-dix-huit.

Address.aufgabe: Ask each other: « Vous habitez où ? » Write down your partner's address. A French address puts the number first and the postcode before the town: 12 rue de la République, 69002 Lyon.

Email and phone number.aufgabe: Dictate an e-mail address and a mobile number to your partner. Your partner writes them down and reads them back.

Forms: nom, prénom, adresse.aufgabe: In pairs, fill in a form for each other: ask, listen, write. On French forms the nom (surname) usually comes before the prénom (first name), often in capitals.
woerter: Écrivez en majuscules, s'il vous plaît.

Family.aufgabe: Draw your family tree and explain it to your partner: « C'est ma mère … »

Married, single ….aufgabe: Ask politely: « Vous êtes marié ? » or « Vous êtes mariée ? » Answer for a person you invent.

Describing people.aufgabe: Describe a person in the class. The others guess who it is. Watch the ending: il est grand, elle est grande.

Rooms.aufgabe: Draw your flat or house. Show your partner around: « Voici la cuisine … »

Furniture.aufgabe: Say what is in your living room. Your partner draws it.
woerter: Dans ma chambre, il y a …

Colours.aufgabe: Find something in the room for every colour and say: « Le sac est bleu. » Watch the ending: le pull vert, la veste verte. Marron and orange never change.

grand / petit / clair.aufgabe: Describe your room with three adjectives. Your partner says if their room is the same.

Food.aufgabe: Write your shopping list for the weekend. Read it to your partner: « J'achète du pain, de la viande … »

Drinks.aufgabe: Ask three people: « Qu'est-ce que tu bois le matin ? » Write down the answers.

Containers (une bouteille de, un paquet.aufgabe: Play shop: one person sells, one person buys. Use « une bouteille de », « un paquet de », « un kilo de ». After a quantity it is always de: un kilo de pommes, not des pommes.
woerter: un kilo de pommes de terre

Prices in euros.aufgabe: Write prices on cards. Your partner asks: « Ça coûte combien ? » and you read the price: 3,50 € = trois euros cinquante. French writes a comma, not a point.

Daily routine.aufgabe: Tell your partner about your morning: « Je me lève à sept heures. Ensuite … »

Times of the day.aufgabe: Say what you do at each time of the day. Your partner says one thing for each, too. In France, lunch is often between noon and 1.30 pm, dinner around 8.

Days of the week.aufgabe: Ask each other: « Qu'est-ce que tu fais lundi ? » Make a plan for the week together. Days have no capital letter in French; le lundi means every Monday.

Hobbies.aufgabe: Ask three people: « Qu'est-ce que tu fais pendant ton temps libre ? » Find one hobby you share.

Sport.aufgabe: Mime a sport. The others guess it: « Tu joues au foot ? » A sport you play is jouer au; a sport you do is faire du / de la.
woerter: aller à la salle de sport

Music.aufgabe: Ask your partner about music: What do they like? Do they play an instrument? An instrument takes jouer du / de la: jouer de la guitare.

The weekend.aufgabe: Plan a weekend together: samedi matin, samedi après-midi, dimanche.

Places in town.aufgabe: Draw a small map of your town. Your partner asks: « Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ? »

Directions.aufgabe: Use the map. Explain the way from the station to the bank. Your partner follows it with a finger.

Transport.aufgabe: Ask three people: « Tu vas au travail comment ? » Count the answers. A vehicle you sit in takes en: en bus, en train; but à pied, à vélo.

Tickets.aufgabe: Role play at the station: buy a ticket to Lyon at the counter or at the machine.
woerter: Un aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
Le train part de quel quai ?

The body.aufgabe: One person says a body part, everyone touches it: « La tête ! » Then a learner takes over.

Illness.aufgabe: Mime an illness. The others guess: « Tu as mal à la tête ? » avoir mal à: j'ai mal à la tête, au dos, aux dents.

At the doctor's (le médecin traitant).aufgabe: Role play at the doctor's: the secretary asks for your carte Vitale, the doctor asks what is wrong. In France you choose a médecin traitant, your regular doctor.

Making an appointment.aufgabe: Role play: phone the surgery and make an appointment. Find a day and a time that works. Many surgeries also take bookings online.
woerter: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.

Everyday actions.aufgabe: Mime something. The others guess with être en train de: « Tu es en train de cuisiner ? » « Oui, je suis en train de cuisiner. »
woerter: je suis en train de travailler

Plans for the weekend.aufgabe: Ask your partner: « Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ? » Tell the class one thing.

aujourd'hui, maintenant, demain.aufgabe: Make a timeline on the board: maintenant, aujourd'hui, ce soir, demain, la semaine prochaine. Everyone adds one sentence.

Jobs.aufgabe: Mime a job. The others guess: « Tu es professeur ? » French has no un or une here: Je suis infirmière.
woerter: Qu'est-ce que vous faites dans la vie ?

Workplaces.aufgabe: Say where people work: « Un professeur travaille dans une école. » Your partner names another job.

Hours and shifts.aufgabe: Ask each other: « Tu commences à quelle heure ? Tu finis à quelle heure ? » Write down the times. Who works in the morning, who at night?
woerter: Je travaille de neuf heures à dix-sept heures.

Clothes.aufgabe: Describe what a person in the class is wearing. The others guess who it is.

Sizes.aufgabe: Role play in a clothes shop: ask for a different size.

Paying.aufgabe: Role play at the till: the customer pays, the shop assistant asks how. Then ask for the receipt.

Months.aufgabe: Line up by birthday, janvier to décembre. Everyone says their month. Months have no capital letter in French.

Festivals.aufgabe: Tell your partner about a festival in your country: When is it? What do people do? Then name one you know in France.

Invitations.aufgabe: Write a short invitation to a party. Your partner says yes or no and gives a reason.

Congratulations.aufgabe: Go round the class: one person names an occasion (a birthday, a new job, a wedding), the next says the right phrase.

Mairie.aufgabe: Role play at the mairie (town hall): ask where the right desk is and what papers you need. The other person works there.
woerter: Je voudrais un renseignement, s'il vous plaît.

Bank.aufgabe: Role play at the bank: open an account or ask about your card.

Forms.aufgabe: Swap forms with your partner and check them: is every box filled in? Is the date right, day first (03/11/2026)?

Proof of address (justificatif de domici.aufgabe: Read the words together. Then role play at a counter (the mairie, the bank, the CAF): you are asked for a justificatif de domicile. This is language practice: which papers are accepted is on the office's own website or on service-public.fr.
woerter: Vous avez un justificatif de domicile ?
